title: personal
description: Per-person constants: the identities, walls, tiering, and standing preferences an orchestrator applies across every repo and org it works in. Names and labels only — never secrets, tokens, or credential values.

version.description: Schema version this file was written against, e.g. "1.0".

contexts.description: The distinct hats this person wears (e.g. personal vs employer-issued). Every git identity, wall, and preference below is scoped to one of these context names.

name.description: Short context label used elsewhere in this file and in repo/org constants, e.g. "personal" or "work".

description.description: One line on what this context covers.

name.description: git user.name for commits made in this context.

email.description: git user.email for commits made in this context.

host_account.description: Code-hosting username/handle attached to this context (e.g. a GitHub login).

runtime_config_dir.description: Optional: the config/home directory a runtime should use when operating in this context (e.g. an alternate CLI config path), if this person runs more than one instance of the same tool.

account_walls.description: Boundaries that must never be crossed by convenience: a runtime billed to the wrong party, an account-scoped tool touching the wrong side. Each wall names the resource, which context owns it, and what to do when a task's context doesn't match.

name.description: Short label for the wall, e.g. the tool or resource class it protects.

kind.description: What kind of boundary this is: who pays, which org/account a tool is scoped to, or a personal subscription that must not be bridged to another runtime.

owning_context.description: Which context (by name, from `contexts`) legitimately owns this resource.

rule.description: The standing rule in one sentence, e.g. "never invoked for the other context's tasks" or "copy config across, never bridge the running instance".

on_violation_risk.description: What to do when a task in the wrong context needs this resource: stop and present options, never improvise around it.

model_tiers.description: Which model class to reach for at each judgment level. Every dispatch should be able to name its tier.

trivial.description: Model/tier for mechanical, low-judgment work (bulk edits, boilerplate).

standard.description: Default model/tier for ordinary delegate work.

judgment.description: Model/tier for work requiring real judgment (architecture, ambiguous tradeoffs).

consultant.description: How the top-of-line model is used, if at all: a small number of single, named-decision-point calls — never as the resident orchestrator. Describe the pattern, not a name.

strategy.description: The default merge strategy for this person's PRs. "merge_commit" means real merge commits, never squashed.

squash_allowed.description: Whether squash merging is ever acceptable. Defaults to false when strategy is merge_commit.

commit_trailer.description: Exact trailer text appended to commits made by an agent on this person's behalf (e.g. a co-authorship line).

review_triage_required.description: Whether triaging automated review-bot comments counts as part of "done" for a PR, separate from checks passing.

communication_preferences.description: Standing preferences about how the orchestrator should communicate, independent of any one task.

topic.description: What the preference is about, e.g. tone, interruption threshold, notification cadence.

preference.description: The preference itself, stated as a rule.

publishing.description: Default channel a skill uses whenever it needs to publish something (a rendered board, a research index, a review) for a person to view outside this conversation. Applies whenever no more specific `tool_mapping` entry for the active context overrides it.

tool_mapping.description: Which concrete tool this person uses for each work-tracking surface, per operating context — so a skill that files or tracks work reads this instead of defaulting to whichever CLI happens to be on hand. One entry per context named in `contexts` above; a context with no entry here falls back to the top-level `publishing` field for publishing and has no tracked default for the others.

context.description: Which context (by name, from `contexts`) this mapping applies to.

tickets.description: The tracker of record for filing and reading work items in this context, and how it's reached (e.g. via a specific CLI rather than its web UI).

docs.description: Where design docs and specs are written and read in this context.

comms.description: Where status updates and questions are posted in this context, if anywhere beyond direct conversation.

publishing.description: Overrides the top-level `publishing` field for this context specifically, if this context needs to publish differently (e.g. one context allows an external channel, another never leaves internal systems).

publishing_channel.description: A pluggable publishing channel. A skill never names a specific one of these in its own text — it reads this block and degrades to the local-file floor when the block is absent or `channel` is "none".

channel.description: "none" (or omitting this block) always falls back to a local file with its path printed — the zero-dependency floor every skill can rely on with no configuration at all. "claude_artifact" only applies inside a session of the assistant product that offers it. "subspace_html_share" publishes a single self-contained file and caps out around 1MB. "heredotnow" is agent-oriented instant publishing (an installable CLI skill or an API); see `heredotnow_mode` for its two tiers. "custom_command" runs whatever command this person supplies.

custom_command.description: Required when channel is "custom_command": the exact command template to run to publish a file (e.g. one that takes a file path and prints back the resulting URL).

heredotnow_mode.description: Only meaningful when channel is "heredotnow". "anonymous" is the free tier (published pages expire after 24h); "api_key" makes the publish permanent, using a key looked up via a credentials tool at the point of use, never stored here.

fallback_note.description: Optional standing note on what the local-file fallback should look like for this person (a preferred directory, a naming convention) — used whenever the configured channel is absent or fails.
